strategy_name: Session-overlap timing — trade high-volume hours, avoid flat off-peak sessions
setup_summary: Falsifiable regime claim: when the London/NY and Asia/London sessions overlap there is higher volume, higher volatility and clearer directional movement; during off-peak hours volume is thin and markets are flat/directionless. The book further claims Tuesday/Wednesday are the most active days and Friday's EU/US overlap is high-volatility, with the second half of Friday unpredictable.
trigger_invalidation: This is a filter, not a directional signal: it gates WHEN to trade (overlap hours, Tue/Wed/Fri-EU/US), not direction. Invalidated regime = off-peak / holiday hours where volume and range contract.
risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target — pure timing regime. Maps to a time-based feature/regime gate on participation.
quote: The binary options market is most active when there is an overlap of the London/New York and Asia/London sessions... During off-peak hours, there is little volume and less price movement, resulting in flat and directionless markets.
chapter_anchor: Fundamentals — Timing: Best time for trading
mechanism: Liquidity and participation cluster at session boundaries, producing cleaner directional moves; thin hours produce noise-dominated, range-bound price action.
notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7 with no session close, so the London/NY overlap framing transfers only partially; however realized volume/volatility on BTC still clusters around US/EU daytime hours and thins on weekends, and funding-period mechanics add their own structure. Claim is stated as 'our research' with no statistics — evidence class NARRATIVE. Candidate input to the existing 'time' feature group.
book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

strategy_name: False breakout reversion
mechanism: liquidity vacuum left by a failed breakout pulls price back through the level
setup_summary: After a congestion zone, price breaks below support to a new low; when the downmove stalls (stops making new lows) and price closes back inside the zone or above the previously broken support line, go long with a protective stop near the latest low. Symmetric for shorts: a false upside breakout to a new high that fails and falls back below the broken resistance gives a sell signal. Short-bar failures at the breakout indicate the move is losing force and the reversion is more likely.
trigger_invalidation: If price keeps making new lows/highs after the false breakout (real breakout resuming), the reversion thesis is invalid; a breakout that never re-enters the congestion zone is a genuine breakout, not a false one.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back above the broken support / into the congestion zone (long), or below the broken resistance (short); stop: below the recent low (near the false-breakout extreme), not at the obvious breakout level; target: the opposite edge of the congestion zone; once the re-entry bar stalls, tighten the stop toward breakeven.
quote: False breakouts are the bane of amateurs, but professional traders love them. They often wait until a downside breakout stops making new lows and then trade against it: buy and place a protective stop near the latest low.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3 (Classical Chart Analysis), Q 3-7, 3-8, 3-10; Answers 3-7, 3-8, 3-10
notes: Confirms and refines the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry). Book adds two refinements: (1) 'wait for the breakout to stop making new extremes' as the entry confirmation, and (2) trading the re-entry into the congestion zone in both directions (the V8 expert is currently SHORT-only). False-breakout signals are frequent on 24/7 perp markets around technical levels.
book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

strategy_name: Trailing stop and stop-loss bail-out rules
mechanism: A stop that trails price by a fixed distance protects accumulated profit while capping loss; a fixed stop-loss activates at a preset price but does not guarantee execution at that price.
setup_summary: Book's concrete rules: (a) stop-loss = sell order triggered at a preset price (e.g., 10% below entry); (b) trailing stop = fixed distance below each new extreme (e.g., 10% below each day's high) — while price rises the stop ratchets up; once price retraces the full distance, exit is generated automatically. Partial-exit variant: pre-set exit points (e.g., close 1/10 of position at each +5%, close all at -10%).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price retraces the trailing distance from the most recent extreme; or price hits the fixed bail-out level. Invalidation: no trailing in place / stop distance not updated at each new extreme; book warns the stop-loss trigger price is not a guaranteed fill ('by the time it was executed, the price had declined to 7.50').
risk_geometry: stop distance = 10% of entry or of the running extreme (book default) — in V8 an ATR-multiple variant; stop refs frozen at bar close per PIT; exit on the trailing-stop bar; combined with per-trade exposure limit (book example: no more than ~10% of capital per trade).
quote: If the stock's price rises, the trailing stop is adjusted to a specified percentage or amount below. As soon as it declines to the 10% level, a sale is generated automatically.
chapter_anchor: Part 8 Seg 4 (stop loss and trailing stop orders; partial exit; RIM gap example)
notes: In 24/7 crypto there are no exchange overnight gaps, so a resting stop is triggered at (near) its level rather than gapping through — this is a genuine improvement over the book's equity-tape caveat. However, the 10% flat distance is crude for high-leverage perps; an ATR-multiple trailing variant is the natural V8 adaptation. Book's trailing-stop-as-profit-protection concept fits the RiskGate/stop family without expanding the active-expert budget.
book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

strategy_name: Support/resistance role flip (breakout validation by retest)
mechanism: A level that previously stopped price becomes the origin of demand/supply after a flip: prior resistance becomes new support after an upside breakout, and prior support becomes new resistance after a downside breakout; the retest of the flipped level validates the breakout.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: after an upside breakout establishes a new, higher range, the old resistance level should act as support — a retest that holds (close stays above the flipped level) validates the breakout and is the entry; mirror for downside where old support becomes resistance. The Coca-Cola example: 'price levels broke through resistance and established a new, higher trading range. The previous resistance price became the new support price.'
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout beyond a windowed range border, then price returns to the border zone (retest) and holds on the new side. Invalidation: the retest closes back through the flipped level (the 'failed breakout' branch of the family applies instead — the level did not flip).
risk_geometry: entry on retest bar close on the flipped side; stop beyond the flipped level; target continuation to a new range; still_valid = close remains on the flipped side; frozen flip-level ref per PIT.
quote: It often occurs that previous resistance becomes new support in an upside breakout; or that previous support becomes resistance in a downside breakout.
chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 1 (b. tests of resistance and support); Part 2 Seg 4 (resistance and support; the 'flip'); Part 3 Seg 2 (flip confirmation)
notes: This is the core thesis of the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family and is intimately related to the active liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert ('stays on reclaimed side'). The book's flip is the retest-after-breakout validation that gives breakout_retest its still_valid semantics. In perps, the flipped level often coincides with a liquidity wall, so the location+liquidity feature groups are the natural input.
book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

strategy_name: Round-number (psychological level) breakout
mechanism: Stop and limit orders cluster at round numbers and 50-pip increments; when a round level breaks, the triggered orders create a sharp burst of directional price action, so break-and-continue in the direction of prevailing sentiment
setup_summary: Identify key round levels (book examples: USD/JPY 105.00, 100.00, 95.00; EUR/USD 1.45, 1.40, 1.35, 1.30) plus 50-increment levels. A sustained break of a round level during active sessions triggers sharp continuation; sell/buy the break in the direction of the prevailing trend or market sentiment rather than fading it. Book notes that during panics one downgrade/level break is often followed by another, so joining beats fading.
trigger_invalidation: The break fails and price closes back through the level; breakouts occurring during the quiet Asian window are predominantly fake-outs (low participation).
risk_geometry: Entry on the break; stop beyond the round level or the data-candle extreme; short-term target in the direction of prevailing sentiment; for news-driven breaks a stop at the data-candle high/low, minimum 20 pips.
quote: Every 100-pip increment will attract stops, and a break of those levels can trigger a sharp burst in price action as brokers process orders that either get their clients into new positions or out of old ones.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Technicals Matter, Too'; Chapter 1 'Turning Headlines into Opportunities'
notes: Transfers directly to crypto: BTC round numbers (50k, 100k) and perp order clustering behave the same way, and the book explicitly warns that quiet-session breaks are fake-outs (see session-timing finding). Mechanism is the same family as liquidity_sweep_reclaim but without the wick-through-reclaim structure - pure break-and-continue on clustered stop liquidity.
book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

strategy_name: Session time-of-day liquidity filter for short-term strategies
mechanism: Breakout and trend strategies need enough participants to fuel continuation; the quiet window (NY close to Europe open, especially the Asian session start) produces fake-outs rather than breakouts
setup_summary: For short-term breakout/momentum strategies, only trust setups when European and U.S. markets are both open (12:00-17:00 GMT overlap); treat breakout signals in the Asian session (approx. NY 5pm-2am) as suspect fake-outs. Book stats: ~70% of the average daily range occurs in European hours and ~80% in U.S. hours. Also: do not range-trade ahead of a big scheduled release - breakout risk is highest there.
trigger_invalidation: A breakout or trend-following signal outside the overlap window is a lower-probability trade; a range break during pre-news dead time is a fake-out risk.
risk_geometry: N/A - timing/admission gate applied to short-term strategies; interacts with the news-surprise rule's 5-minute wait.
quote: This is the time when more 'fake-outs' than breakouts occur because the beginning of the Asian session is typically one of the quietest times in the currency market.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Zones'; Chapter 10, 'If You're a Short-Term Trader...'
notes: Maps directly to 24/7 crypto: BTC ranges compress in the Asian window and breakouts there are disproportionately fake-outs, while the London/NY overlap is the high-volume window. Time is a frozen V8 feature group; this becomes a time-gated lifecycle rule (episode admission by session), not a separate expert.
book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

strategy_name: Thin-market liquidity avoidance
mechanism: low participation widens spreads and degrades fill quality, so execution cost in an inactive market exceeds the small tradable range available
setup_summary: Do not open positions in structurally illiquid windows: Friday afternoon, weekends, session close, bank holidays, end of December, overnight. These windows offer smaller ranges and wider spreads; price can be chaotic and stops unreliable.
trigger_invalidation: Applies when liquidity is structurally low; a rolling spread/liquidity measure could gate admission in place of a fixed clock for a 24/7 market.
risk_geometry: No entry geometry - a time- or liquidity-based admission gate at the lifecycle layer.
quote: An inactive (often called 'thin') market offers smaller movements of rates, thus smaller potential profits. A thin market also comes with higher commissions (spreads) for each trade due to the decreased liquidity.
chapter_anchor: Section 03, When NOT to trade forex
notes: Crypto perps have no weekend close and no central session clock, so the fixed-clock version does not transfer; but BTC weekend books are genuinely thinner, so a liquidity-based (spread/order-book-depth) admission gate is the honest 24/7 adaptation. Book also lists 'when angry or frustrated' and overnight as avoid windows - psychological/execution-state admissions that are harder to formalize deterministically.
book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

strategy_name: Session-overlap volatility timing
mechanism: liquidity and participation cluster at session overlaps, concentrating volatility and tradable range into a few daily windows
setup_summary: Concentrate analysis and entries in the high-participation windows: the London/New-York overlap (~10:00 EST, when London closes and the US opens) provides the biggest returns, with 20-30 pips of opportunity in Euro pairs at the London open; the biggest weekly moves in the four majors occur Tuesday and Wednesday, and Friday is only tradeable until ~12:00.
trigger_invalidation: Timing filter only; invalidated per instrument if no hourly volatility differential is observed.
risk_geometry: No entry geometry - a timing filter to run alongside entries; needs time-derived features (hour of day, session label) on the tape.
quote: The time when the London session intersects with the US session usually provides the biggest returns. ... the biggest movement in the four major currency pairs ... is observed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
chapter_anchor: Section 03, What Are the Best Times to Trade Forex
notes: Crypto is 24/7 with no formal sessions, but BTC volatility/volume still clusters around US daytime and the funding-rate window; the overlap concept maps to participation concentration, not the FX session structure. V8's 'time' feature group could host a session/participation feature. Book claims 'according to research' for Tuesday/Wednesday but presents no statistics.
book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

strategy_name: Kangaroo tail / tested-and-rejected level (wick rejection)
mechanism: a long wick through a level that closes back on the other side shows the level was swept and rejected, trapping the sweepers and fueling the recoil
setup_summary: A 'kangaroo tail' — a bar whose wick spikes through a support/resistance level and closes back on the reclaimed side — marks a level that has been tested and rejected; prices recoil from tails. Buy the rejection of a downside wick through support; short the rejection of an upside wick through resistance. A tail can also serve as the first low of a double bottom.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = wick through a windowed prior extreme with close back on the reclaimed side. Invalidate = close stays beyond the level (sweep not rejected / reclaim fails).
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after reclaim; stop beyond the tail's extreme (the swept wick); target = opposite structure (double-bottom objective / channel).
quote: Tails... show what levels prices have tested and rejected. Prices recoil from kangaroo tails.
chapter_anchor: Answer 22; Answer 28 ('The kangaroo tail B serves as the first low of a double bottom'); Answer 33
notes: Corroborates V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim. High-leverage perp markets produce abundant wick-through-reclaim tails (liquidation sweeps) on 1h bars; funding-mark boundaries may cluster sweep events and are a time-feature to test.
book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as continuation and S/R zones
mechanism: a window is a price vacuum where no trades occurred; unfilled price levels magnetize price and act as support/resistance on corrections - 'corrections stop at the window'
setup_summary: A rising window (gap up: no overlap between the prior bar's high and the current bar's low) is a bullish continuation whose entire zone is support, most critically the window bottom; a falling window is bearish continuation with resistance at the window top. Size is irrelevant - even a 1-tick window counts. Break of window support requires a close under the bottom; once breached, the window is voided.
trigger_invalidation: A close through the window's critical edge voids it (once a rising window's support is broken, it is no longer support on a later rally); the book explicitly warns against fading large gaps (high risk).
risk_geometry: Entry: on a pullback into the window holding on a close. Stop: below window bottom (rising) / above window top (falling). Break by close voids the level and shifts attention to the next window or structure.
quote: 'Corrections stop at the window.' That means windows often become support and resistance areas... the most important area of a rising window is the bottom of that window.
chapter_anchor: Ch3 S4 (pp.101-110), Ch5 (breakaway-gap exhibits), Ch4 Guidelines (p.122)
notes: In continuous 24/7 perp markets, true price vacuums between consecutive bars are rare except during liquidation cascades or venue halts; funding does not create gaps. The vacuum logic overlaps the liquidity_vacuum mechanism already used by failed_breakout. Defer; if ever implemented, treat the window as a vacuum level rather than an exchange gap.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Trend Knockout (stop-hunt re-entry)
mechanism: In a strong trend, a two-bar low knocks out weak hands and stop holders; the resulting vacuum lets the trend resume
setup_summary: Strong trend (ADX>=30 with +DMI>-DMI, or Trend Qualifiers). The market makes at least a two-bar low (trades below the prior two bars' lows). Buy next day or the day after, 1/16 above today's high; protective stop below the low of the knockout bar, capped at 5% of price.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above the prior bar's high within 1-2 bars after a 2+ bar low in a strong trend. Invalidation: trade below the knockout-bar low; deeper 3+ bar knockouts are considered stronger but less fillable.
risk_geometry: Entry: stop-order 1/16 above current bar high, valid up to 2 bars. Stop: 1/16 below low of the knockout bar, max 5% risk. Target: trend continuation; 2-for-1 scale-out, ~7-bar time stop.
quote: Trend Knockouts (TKOs) identify strong trends from which the weak hands have already been knocked out. By placing your order above the market, you have the potential to capture profits as the trend resumes.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Fakeouts and False Moves - Trend Knockouts (pp. 62-67)
notes: New expert family; mechanism matches V8's liquidity lexicon ('stop-run creates vacuum'). Complementary to liquidity_sweep_reclaim but close-based (2-bar low) rather than wick-through-extreme. Corroborated by the book's repeated lesson that second entries after being stopped out are often the best entries.
book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

strategy_name: Support and resistance level role-flip
setup_summary: Support is defined (glossary) as a price floor at which the exchange rate 'automatically corrects itself'; the index shows the book formalizes the game of scoring points at highs/lows (Ch.5, pp.71-87) including 'Past Resistance can Become Future Support' (p.83) and 'Past Support can Become Future Resistance' (p.84). Falsifiable: after a prior high is broken, that level flips from resistance to support and price is expected to halt/bounce there.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaches a prior extreme that has been broken in the direction of travel. Invalidation: price closes cleanly through the flipped level without a reaction.
risk_geometry: Level-based entries at prior swing extremes; stops beyond the flipped level (structure), target at the next prior extreme.
quote: Support Levels A technique used in technical analysis that indicates a specific price ceiling and floor at which a given exchange rate will automatically correct itself.
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'Support Levels'; Index pp.75-84 (Ch.5 The Financial Game of Support and Resistance)
notes: Role-flip of levels is the same behavioral claim V8's location feature group feeds; 24/7 trading with no exchange gaps makes level tests cleaner (no gap-through ambiguity), though high leverage increases stop-run frequency at these levels.
book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

strategy_name: Buy zone / sell zone entries
setup_summary: Chapter 7 (pp.113-127) splits the chart into a sell zone (short the market when price enters it, p.121) and a buy zone (go long when price enters it, p.126), with zones divided by trend lines (p.117). Falsifiable: entries are only taken at the zone edge defined by the prevailing trend line, not mid-zone.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price enters the zone of interest against the trend. Invalidation: price trades back through the zone's defining trend line (trend-line break, p.126).
risk_geometry: Zone-edge entry; index references 'trend line division of, 117' and bullish-candle entrance for buy zones (p.122); stop on the far side of the trend-line divider.
quote: Shorting the Market When It Enters the Sell Zone, 121
chapter_anchor: Index pp.113-127 (Ch.7 Buy and Sell Zones)
notes: Zone-plus-trend-line structure is implementable on 1h BTC, but trend-line construction is discretionary; the exact zone definitions are in Part 1. Corroborates the location feature group and the supply_demand_zone backlog.
book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

strategy_name: Double Top/Bottom stop-run excess penetration
mechanism: in double tops/bottoms the second extreme slightly exceeds the first to take out clustered stop orders placed at/beyond the level, then reverses; the excess penetration is a liquidity artifact
setup_summary: Classical Double Bottom/Top: the second low just barely ticks through the first low (or the second high through the first high) before reversing - stops placed just at/beyond the extreme are 'taken out just as the market reverses'. Trend clues: wide range bars on the reversal side, first retracement only reaching .382 (sign of a trend). Trade the reversal long after the stop-run on the second low, or trade the failure point (break beyond the pattern extreme = explosive continuation) via buy-stop/sell-stop orders.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: second extreme wicks through the first and reverses with wide bars. Invalidated: the extreme breaks cleanly without reversal (failure point), which then becomes a continuation entry in the breakdown direction.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at .618 retracement of the reversal move or buy-stop above the failure point; a smaller timeframe can time the entry. Stop: below the pattern low / beyond the failure level; profit taken at .382 retracement, stop to breakeven. Failure point of double top = the pattern high; double bottom = the pattern low.
quote: It is not unusual for the second low on a Double Bottom pattern to be exceeded by a small amount... stops are placed just at or slightly beyond these levels and are taken out just as the market reverses.
chapter_anchor: Ch 9, Pattern Recognition (Double Top and Bottom)
notes: Directly corroborates the V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim family mechanism (liquidity_vacuum_reentry): a wick through a prior extreme that is reclaimed by close. 'Second low ticks through first low' is a concrete, testable feature on 1h BTC. Stop clusters near swing extremes are prominent in perps with liquidation cascades.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Round Number Fade (Fading the Double Zeros)
mechanism: Take-profit orders cluster at psychologically round numbers while stops sit just beyond them, so price is magnetized to the level and stop-gunning by banks produces a contra-trend bounce.
setup_summary: On a 10-15 minute chart (adapt to 1h), price trades well below (long side) its 20-period SMA and approaches a psychological round number (book examples 105.00 USD/JPY, 1.2800 EUR/USD; in BTC, 100000/50000-style levels); enter a few pips (<=10) before the figure, stop <=20 pips, first-half target 2R, then trail. Filter: level gains weight when it coincides with a Fibonacci retracement, moving average, or Bollinger band, and when no major scheduled economic release is imminent.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches the entry zone while 20-SMA displacement is intact. Invalidation: stop hit (decisive move through the round number by >20 pips with momentum, implying real orders rather than cluster-fades); thesis dead if the figure breaks cleanly.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit a few pips (<=10) before the figure; initial stop 20 pips; take half at 2x risk, move stop to breakeven, trail remainder (book uses two-bar low / five-bar low); intraday expiry.
quote: While stop-loss orders are usually placed just beyond the round numbers, traders will cluster their lake-profit orders at the round number.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Fading the Double Zeros', p. 81-85
notes: Round-number psychology survives in crypto (100k BTC, prior structural round levels) but the 'bank dealer guns clustered stops' mechanism is weaker in an all-visible central-limit order book; the magnet/reversal frequency around round levels is falsifiable on BTCUSDT. Needs sub-1h bars or a 1h adaptation (20-SMA displacement + round-level proximity).
book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

strategy_name: Waiting for the Real Deal (session-open stop-hunt fake-out)
mechanism: At the London open the initial range-break is a deliberate stop-hunt to clear books; once those stops are run, the real directional move follows.
setup_summary: Define the Frankfurt-London 'power hour' range (1-2 a.m. EST). Long setup: GBP/USD makes a new range low at least 25 pips below the range high, then reverses and penetrates the range high; enter buy 10 pips above the range high with a stop <=20 pips; first-half target 2R, then trail by two-bar low. Short is the mirror. Works best following the U.S. open or after a major economic release once the noise has settled.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: range low/high made by >=25 pips then reclaimed. Invalidation: stop hit; no reversal penetration within the session.
risk_geometry: Entry: 10 pips beyond range high/low; stop <=20 pips; first lot at 2R, move to breakeven, trail remainder (two-bar high/low).
quote: Once these stops are taken out and the books are cleared, the real directional move in the GBP/USD will begin to occur.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Waiting for the Real Deal', p. 85-88
notes: Crypto has no discrete London open; the pattern must be re-expressed as 'first range-break is a fake-out, reversal then real move' around high-volume transition windows (Asia->Europe, UTC 6-12). Session ranges map to ATR-scaled ranges; needs a time-of-day feature group.
book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

strategy_name: The Fader (fade false breakouts in range)
mechanism: In a range-bound environment with weak ADX, breakouts beyond the prior day's range are traps; fading the failed breakout captures the reversion (liquidity vacuum then refill).
setup_summary: Range-bound regime (ADX(14) < 35, ideally declining; daily chart defines the range, hourly charts for entries). Long: wait for a break below the previous day's low by >=15 pips (false breakout), then buy 15 pips above the previous day's high; stop <=30 pips; target 60 pips (2R). Short is the mirror. Stand aside around major scheduled economic releases and on volatile pairs.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prior-day level violated by >=15 pips then reclaimed; entry on reclaim 15 pips beyond the other side. Invalidation: 30-pip stop; 2R target; skip if ADX >35 or a scheduled release looms.
risk_geometry: Entry: 15 pips beyond prior-day high/low; stop 30 pips; target 2R (60 pips); fixed 2R, no trailing prescribed.
quote: Wait for the market to break below the previous day's low by at least 15 pips. Place an entry order to buy 15 pips above the previous day's high.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'The Fader', p. 92-94
notes: Directly refines V8's failed_breakout expert: adds the ADX<35 range filter, the 15-pip false-break threshold, the 30-pip stop and 2R target, and the no-news-day filter. The existing V8 variant covers the SHORT-after-failed-high case; the book adds the symmetric long side and the same-side re-entry rule.
book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

strategy_name: Economic Release Timing and Event-Window Discipline
mechanism: Scheduled macro releases produce a concentrated, fast price adjustment (most of it within the first 20 minutes); reactions beyond 15-30 minutes are overreaction/flow, and trading systematic strategies through high-impact releases is negative-expectancy.
setup_summary: Rank scheduled releases by historical post-release range (book's 2004 EUR/USD table: NFP 124 pips in first 20 min / 193 pips daily vs GDP 43/110; FOMC 74/140). No new systematic exposure during the release window; disable system strategies ahead of the highest-mover releases (NFP). Breakout traders can weight position size by expected release range (50% size for a GDP-day breakout vs NFP-day).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled-release calendar event. Invalidation: window closes (15-30 min post-release) and the move has been made.
risk_geometry: No price geometry; lifecycle rule: flat ahead of high-impact events, re-enable after the adjustment window.
quote: many system traders turn their systems off ahead of big releases such as the U.S. nonfarm payrolls reports.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4, 'What Moves the Currency Market in the Short Term?', p. 46-49
notes: The book's 2004 study of post-release pip ranges is a falsifiable empirical case (LITERATURE_SUPPORTED). In 24/7 crypto perps there is no closing bell to protect you, so a scheduled-event lifecycle rule (flat through FOMC/CPI/NFP windows) is directly applicable and reinforces the event/available/ingested clock discipline.
book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

strategy_name: Fade the false breakout (slingshot against a fakeout / premature break)
mechanism: Most major breakouts are false: a level is breached slightly then price reverses, trapping breakout traders; a false breakout against the prevailing trend has a high failure rate and sets up a slingshot move in the opposite direction (vacuum created by trapped stops).
setup_summary: Observe a breakout of a significant horizontal support/resistance, trendline, or pattern. If the break fails — price reverses back through the level with no follow-through (fakeout) or reverses after a premature break and then re-breaks — fade it: trade opposite the failed break. Ed Ponsi specifically favors false breakouts that move against the prevailing trend.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: false/premature break with price back through the level. Invalidation: the break proves true and carries real directional momentum; stop must be placed beyond the false-break extreme.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back on the original side of the broken level. Stop: beyond the false-break extreme/high-water mark of the trap. Target: opposite side of range or prior structure; book stresses proper risk controls because fading 'goes directly against the trend and momentum'.
quote: One of my favorite situations is a false breakout that moves against the trend. These types of breakouts have a high failure rate, and they also set the stage for a 'slingshot' trade in the opposite direction.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Breakout Trading (and Fading)' pp.150-153; Ed Ponsi Executive Insight pp.157-158
notes: Matches the existing V8 failed_breakout family (liquidity_vacuum_reentry, SHORT, close-below-windowed-prior-high, frozen ref). Book's additional claim: a false break AGAINST the prevailing trend (not just any false break) is the highest-quality slingshot — a candidate refinement: require the fakeout to oppose higher-TF trend. Highly relevant to crypto where leveraged stop cascades amplify the vacuum.
book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

strategy_name: Day-of-week risk (weekday edge patterns around weekly expiration)
mechanism: calendar flow rotation: day-of-week microstructure (weekly expiration cycle, weekend behavior) creates systematic weekday-specific edge patterns

strategy_name: Fade the Break (false-break candle at support/resistance)
mechanism: A wick through a level that fails to hold on close is an institutional trap that catches retail breakout traders (liquidity-vacuum reentry), so the reclaiming close predicts reversal back inside the level.
setup_summary: On M15/M30, identify a clear support/resistance level (at least two touches). A candle's wick pierces the level but closes back on the inside (bull candle above support / bear candle below resistance) = false-break candle. Enter at the opening of the next candle in the reclaim direction; stop 5 pips beyond the false-break candle's extreme; two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the candle closes beyond the level (genuine close-through, not a wick) or no candle forms a wick-through-reclaim; dead thesis if price closes decisively through the level on a subsequent candle or the 5-pip-beyond-extreme stop is hit.
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open; stop 5 pips beyond the false-break candle high/low; dual targets 1R and 2R; no expiry stated (intraday M15/M30 day-trade profile).
quote: Markets often reverse after a failure to break above the resistance level or below the support level. ... the failure is characterized by the shadow of the candle that goes above the resistance level but fails to close above it.

strategy_name: Guppy Burst (quiet-window range breakout with dual pending orders)
mechanism: After the US close, liquidity thins and price compresses into a tight range; the subsequent Asia-open breakout is a genuine liquidity release, so resting buy-stop at the range high and sell-stop at the range low catch whichever side resolves, with the stop at the opposite extreme.
setup_summary: On M5 GBP/JPY, in the ~3-hour window after the US market close (before Asia opens), record the highest high and lowest low of the window. Place both a pending buy-stop at the high and a pending sell-stop at the low; stop at the opposite side of the range; target = 2x the range height (1:2 R, e.g., 30-pip range -> 60-pip target). When one pending order triggers, cancel the other immediately.
trigger_invalidation: Range must come from the quiet window only; once one pending fills, the other must be deleted (no double exposure); stopped if price reverses through the full range; trade only during the 3-hour gap (one setup per day).
risk_geometry: Entry: pending buy/sell stop at range extremes; stop at the opposite extreme; target 2x the range (1:2 R); expiry: intraday session.
quote: The guppy burst seeks to identify the trading range during this 3-hour window and anticipate a potential breakout of the trading range.

notes: The dual-pending-order pattern is a deterministic structure worth encoding, but the exact '3-hour gap after US close' session anchor does not exist in 24/7 perps (no close/open, no gaps). The adaptable analog is a low-liquidity/low-volatility window (e.g., late weekend, funding-time compression). strategy_name: Spring (break of support then reclaim); mirror upthrust
setup_summary: After an important support area, price breaks under it then 'springs' back above the broken level — the reclaim is the trigger (LONG). The mirror 'upthrust' setup: price breaks through important resistance, fails to hold the new highs, and pulls back under the pierced resistance (SHORT).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = bar close back above the broken support (spring) or close back under the pierced resistance (upthrust). Thesis invalid if the reclaimed side is re-crossed.
risk_geometry: Book gives no numeric geometry in this section; freeze the swept extreme as reference, entry on close of the reclaim bar, stop beyond the swept extreme.

strategy_name: Good trade versus winning trade (evaluate process, not outcome)
mechanism: Single-trade outcomes are noise; a strategy is judged by whether the predetermined plan was followed, because a winning outcome can follow broken rules and a losing outcome can follow perfect execution.
setup_summary: Evaluation rule: episode attribution goes to adherence to the plan (stop placed correctly, defined exit), never to the realized PnL of the trade; the trader should 'strive to be a good trader,' not a lucky one.
trigger_invalidation: If a plan is followed perfectly and still loses over a large frozen-OOS sample, the fault is with the plan and the plan is modified — not the execution.
risk_geometry: None — evaluation principle.

strategy_name: Change of polarity: broken support becomes resistance and vice versa
mechanism: a level tested often accumulates resting orders; once broken those orders flip side and magnetize price back for a rejection test
setup_summary: Identify a level tested at least twice as support (or resistance). After a close below it, the level flips to resistance; a bearish candle (hanging man, dark cloud cover, shooting star, long upper shadow) forming at the flipped level is a short entry. Mirror for broken resistance flipping to support. The more tests before the break, the stronger the expected flip.
trigger_invalidation: A close back beyond the flipped level invalidates the thesis; if no rejection signal appears at the flipped level within a few bars, abandon the setup.
risk_geometry: Entry on the candle-signal close at the flipped level; stop on a close beyond the flipped level; target = next support / prior congestion / measured move.
quote: a penetrated resistance area should then be converted to support and a broken support area should be resistance... the more often a support or resistance area is tested before prices break them, the better the change of polarity principle should work.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Hanging Man' (change of polarity), pp.62-64

strategy_name: Exit discipline and mandatory stop-loss (The Experiment / three points in every trade)

In the book's controlled experiment, two traders with identical capital, entries, and trade count diverged to 10% vs 2% monthly return solely because one meddled with exits (exited 'too impatiently').

strategy_name: Busted Pattern (Failed Breakout) with Bust Counting
mechanism: liquidity vacuum reentry: a pattern that breaks out its normal way, fails, and closes through the opposite boundary re-enters with momentum; single/double/triple bust counts quantify how often and how reliably
setup_summary: A chart pattern that breaks out, then price closes back into the pattern and breaks out the other way is a 'busted' pattern. Falsifiable claims from the book: single busts occur ~23% of the time for double tops in bull markets, double and triple busts ~5% each; single-busted patterns perform as good as or better than their non-busted counterparts; rectangles that single bust gain on average more than non-busted ones. This is the book's name for V8's failed_breakout mechanism, with bust-count as an added variant dimension.
trigger_invalidation: On the first bust, a stop placed beyond the original pattern boundary takes the loss; re-entry only on a confirmed opposite-direction close-through, with the bust count (1st/2nd/3rd failure attempt) gating the trade.
risk_geometry: Entry on confirmed opposite breakout (close through the boundary); stop beyond the opposite side of the pattern; bust-count acts as a variant parameter that can gate entry quality.

strategy_name: The Stop Run: fade the false breakout against the trend
mechanism: a pool of stop orders above a well-tested resistance acts as a magnet; banks/institutions push price through the level to execute the order cluster, the breakout then fails once the orders are consumed, and trapped breakout longs covering at a loss supply the fuel for trend resumption
setup_summary: In an established trend (the book's example: USD/CAD downtrend with repeated rejections at Fibonacci resistance 1.1250), a stop-run pushes price above the resistance level; if price falls back beneath the breakout point within a short window (two hours in the example), enter in the direction of the primary trend. The unwinding of breakout traders' losing longs supplies selling pressure.
trigger_invalidation: No entry if the breakout succeeds and holds above the level; thesis invalid if price re-crosses back above the broken level after entry.
risk_geometry: Entry on the return below the broken level; stop above the failed-breakout high (and above the resistance/Fibonacci level); exits via the multi-exit scheme (partial at 1R, stop to breakeven, remainder at prior support).
quote: Breakouts that run in the opposite direction of the trend have a greater likelihood of failure... I would consider the breakout to have failed if the exchange rate falls back beneath the breakout point of 1.1250.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 'The Stop Run', pp.91-97
notes: Directly matches the existing failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry). The book adds the causal mechanism: stop clusters above resistance attract execution pushes (more likely during quiet/low-liquidity times), and the trapped breakout longs' covering is the continuation fuel. On crypto perps this mechanism is amplified by liquidation cascades and the absence of exchange gaps; the 'pool of orders' magnet argument is a liquidity feature, not just a location pattern.

strategy_name: Position trading over day trading (big moves, 80/20)
mechanism: Holding-period return concentration: multi-day position trading captured >80% of profit while consuming far less time than day trading; a hard time budget (15 min/day) forces execution over overthinking, and more screen time correlated with worse position-trading results.
setup_summary: Split trading into day trades (<1 day) vs position trades (held overnight, usually several days). Author's analysis: position trading accounted for over 80% of yearly profit while day trading was under 20% despite all-day effort; his position trading was more profitable when he spent less time on it (overthinking, analysis paralysis, early exits).

risk_geometry: None — timeframe/methodology. Implies multi-day holding (expiry in days, not hours).

strategy_name: 1.13 failed-wave stop run (nominal breach of prior extreme then reversal)
mechanism: Nominal breach of a prior extreme to the 1.13 extension of the last leg is a failed breakout/breakdown stop run that reverses; exceeding the 1.13 signals continuation to the 1.27 or 1.618 areas.
setup_summary: After an extended down leg, price bounces quickly then rolls over to a nominal new low at the 1.13 extension of the prior leg and reverses; mirror for tops. The 1.13 defines the sweep depth — if price exceeds 1.13, the rule of thumb is continuation to 1.27/1.618 rather than reversal.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price taps the 1.13 extension of a prior leg at a prior extreme and reverses. Invalid: close beyond 1.13 (then the continuation rule applies); reversal candidate requires the failed-wave structure (void of distinct harmonic pattern).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at the 1.13 extension; stop just beyond 1.13; target: reversal; or flip to a continuation trade toward 1.27/1.618 if 1.13 is exceeded. Author notes this was adopted precisely to avoid stop-outs just before reversals.
quote: It has been my experience that price action that exceeds a critical 1.13 extension level frequently will continue farther to the 1.27 or 1.618 areas.

notes: Directly refines the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim family by quantifying sweep depth (1.13) and adding the exceeding-1.13 continuation rule — a concrete falsifiable addition. High leverage in perps clusters stops at prior extremes, so the mechanism is structurally active on BTC.

strategy_name: Harmonic PRZ violation as continuation (failed pattern, 0.886 target)
mechanism: Violation of a fully-tested harmonic PRZ creates a liquidity vacuum: price accelerates in the primary trend direction to at least the 0.886 retracement beyond the completion point.
setup_summary: After a harmonic pattern's entire PRZ has been tested, a violation — especially on a second test after a nominal first-test reaction — is a continuation trade with the primary trend, targeting at least the 0.886 retracement beyond the pattern completion. The 2000/2008 case studies are the book's core evidence (failed monster bullish Gartley and 5-0 → acceleration of downtrends).

risk_geometry: Entry: bar close after PRZ violation; target: minimum 0.886 retracement beyond completion; stop: back above/below the violated PRZ; continuation typically accelerates after brief consolidation.

strategy_name: Signal Crowding Degrades Entry (capacity lesson)
mechanism: When many traders run the identical signal, the shared order flow concentrates at one price and the entry degenerates into gap-and-run or gap-and-collapse; edge depends on crowding, so risk and order flow should be diversified across many independent strategies.

Neither outcome is profitable for the crowd.

risk_geometry: None stated.
quote: Either KLAC will gap up and over 50.00 and not look back, or it will gap open at 50.00, run up a bit, then collapse once all that volume is assimilated. Neither scenario provides a proﬁtable trading environment.

The wide spread without volume participation is a trap; enter the opposite direction once the trap move fails and price closes back through its origin. Stop beyond the trap wick.

risk_geometry: Entry bar close on failure of the trap move; stop beyond the trap extreme wick; target prior congestion on the opposite side.

strategy_name: Low-volume long-legged doji stop-hunt (news/event whipsaw) - stand aside
mechanism: a violently volatile bar (long-legged doji) on LOW volume is anomalous - price is being 'racked' to take out stops and limits with insiders not participating; low volume on a wide move proves it is engineered, not genuine.
setup_summary: During/around a news or event release, price swings violently one way then the other and closes near the open, printing a long-legged doji; if the volume is LOW this is an anomaly and a stop-hunt/trap - the book's instruction is to stay out and wait for later candles. Corollary: any event-driven price move must be validated by rising volume; a wide move on low volume means the insiders are not joining.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: long-legged doji (or wide two-way move) on low volume around an event. Invalidation: doji validated by average-or-higher volume (genuine indecision, watch for follow-through), or subsequent candles confirm a direction on volume.
risk_geometry: None - this is a stay-out filter, not an entry. Book: 'we stay out, and wait for further candles to unfold.'
quote: The most common reason for this is stop hunting, where the market makers and insiders are moving prices violently, first one way and then the other, to shake traders out, and to take out stop and limit orders in the process.

strategy_name: Failed breakout at resistance (intraday breach not sustained by the close / upper-wick rejection)
mechanism: Price breaches a level intraday but closes back inside/under it, leaving an upper shadow; the failed attempt reveals insufficient demand at that level and unresolved liquidity to the downside.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, price trades above a windowed prior high (or consolidation ceiling) intraday but closes below that level, printing a long upper shadow / shooting star at the level (a failed breakout attempt). The short signal triggers after the failed breakout, with the level frozen as the resistance reference.
trigger_invalidation: If price closes above the level (breakout confirmed), the failed-breakout thesis is invalid. A pattern forming in a long consolidation with no directional move to reverse weakens the signal. The book also shows the mirror: repeated wick tests of a strong visible ceiling get retested until the level is finally broken.
risk_geometry: Existing V8 expert geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE below the frozen ref, target_r 1.0, stop_r 1.0, expiry_bars 8, atr_ref; still_valid = close stays below ref. Book adds that multiple wick tests of a ceiling strengthen the level and that a 'strong and visible ceiling' will be reacted to repeatedly.
quote: Price actually broke out just slightly above the April high intraday, but closed below it, resulting in a failed breakout attempt.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Tails at Support and Resistance, p.93; Ch 4, Figure 4.1, p.80
notes: Closest match in this book to an already-formalized V8 expert (failed_breakout / liquidity_vacuum_reentry). Refinement inputs: (1) wick-penetration depth vs close-side condition as the trigger, (2) multi-touch ceiling strength, (3) doji-at-resistance variant.

strategy_name: Outcome-independent execution protocol
setup_summary: Execution and evaluation follow a pre-committed protocol that does not vary with the last outcome: the same rules run whether the last five episodes won or lost. Ancient evaluation judged heroes by actions, not results, and dignity is the execution of a behavior protocol independent of immediate circumstance.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology principle, not a tradable setup; falsifiable only as process adherence (episode scores should record protocol compliance separately from outcome).
risk_geometry: None.
quote: dignity defined as the execution of a protocol of behavior that does not depend on the immediate circumstance
chapter_anchor: Ch. 14 'Bacchus Abandons Antony' (p. 192)

strategy_name: Stop hunting / post-breach momentum (Osler)
setup_summary: Stops cluster at support/resistance and at round numbers near price. Once price pierces the level, the triggered sell (buy) stops push price further down (up) for a while; HFTs can also preemptively push price toward the level to ignite the cascade and cover. Falsifiable on BTCUSDT 1h: after a bar closes beyond a windowed prior swing level or a psychological round number, measure forward drift over the next K bars against a baseline.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: bar close beyond a prior swing support/resistance or round-number level. Invalidation: thesis is continuation-after-stop-run; invalidated if price reverts back inside the range within K bars (no vacuum), or if the breach occurs on declining stop-cluster density.
risk_geometry: Entry at NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after breach; stop = back inside the broken level (swing point); target = next structure (R-multiple 1.0); expiry = K bars (book's time-based exits).
quote: Research in the currencies markets indicated that once support (resistance) levels are breached, prices will go further down (up) for a while (Osler, 2000, 2001).
chapter_anchor: Ch 7 High-Frequency Trading, pp.167-168 (stop hunting, Osler citation)
notes: Cites Osler's empirical intraday FX work on post-breach continuation driven by stop clustering. Crypto perp: 24/7 stops always live, high leverage inflates stop clusters, and round-number/liquidation levels matter; 1h-bar testable. Overlaps the formalized failed_breakout / liquidity_sweep_reclaim families; the new element is the round-number location feature and the pre-breach manipulation narrative (HFT-only, not directly tradeable by us).

strategy_name: Calendar-spread / term-structure mean reversion on roll return gamma, and spot-vs-future roll extraction
mechanism: the log calendar spread equals gamma*(T1-T2); its signal depends only on the mean-reverting roll return gamma, not on the spot, so carry reversion is tradeable separately from price
setup_summary: Long-far/short-near calendar spread: log value = gamma*(T1-T2), so the spread signal is driven entirely by gamma (estimated by regressing log futures prices on time-to-maturity). CL 12-month calendar spread: ADF stationary at 99%, half-life 36 days, linear mean-reversion APR 8.3%, Sharpe 1.3. Equivalent spot-extraction trade: buy the underlying asset (or a producer ETF) and short the future under contango, reverse in backwardation (GLD vs GC: 1.9% annualized, max DD 0.8%; XLE-USO: APR 16%). Crypto analog: perp (spot-anchored) vs quarterly futures basis and persistent funding.
trigger_invalidation: gamma stops mean-reverting (persistently one-sided term structure); the underlying is not a tradeable asset (VX case: model 5.7 breaks).
risk_geometry: Roll to next contract pair 10 days before near expiry; ~3-month holding; signal reversal when z-score of gamma crosses zero.
quote: the calendar spread trading signal does not depend at all on the spot price, only on the roll return!
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Trading Futures Calendar Spread' (Example 5.4) + Chapter 6, 'Extracting Roll Returns through Future versus ETF Arbitrage'

strategy_name: Buy-on-gap: seasonal intraday mean reversion with a momentum filter (reversion only when above the MA)
mechanism: liquidity-demand selling at a session open overshoots and reverts, but only when the drop is not news-driven; the long-term-MA filter separates the two
setup_summary: At market open, select stocks whose open is more than 1 std (90-day close-to-close) below the previous day's low (gapped down) AND whose open is above the 20-day moving average of closes; buy the 10 lowest, liquidate at the close. SPX backtest: APR 8.7%, Sharpe 1.5 (2006-2012). Mirror short version (gap up, below MA): APR 46%, Sharpe 1.27, steeper drawdown. Key transferable idea: price series that show no mean reversion on daily closes can show strong mean reversion in specific periods/sessions ('seasonal' or time-conditioned mean reversion); the momentum filter (price above a longer MA) keeps out drops caused by real news.
trigger_invalidation: Open below the MA (news-driven drop, no reversion); panic selling does not finish intraday; open-close drift turns negative.
risk_geometry: Entry at session open (uses preopen prices - signal noise acknowledged), exit at close; ~10 positions, intraday, no overnight.
quote: on days when the stock index futures are down before the open, certain stocks suffer disproportionately due to panic selling at the open. But once this panic selling is over, the stock will gradually appreciate over the course of the day.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Intraday Mean Reversion: Buy-on-Gap Model' (Example 4.1)
notes: Crypto has no opening auction or exchange gaps (24/7), so the literal gap setup does not translate. The transferable lessons are (a) time-conditioned/seasonal mean reversion as a V8 time-of-day feature, and (b) the momentum-filter-on-mean-reversion technique that 'reprises often' in the book - a strong FEATURE_INPUT for the mean_reversion_band family.

strategy_name: Catalog of execution errors (fear/euphoria/self-valuation driven)
mechanism: Loss of objectivity manifests as a specific enumerable set of execution errors rather than analysis failures; the mechanical regime is designed to eliminate exactly these
setup_summary: The book enumerates the error set a trader becomes susceptible to when objectivity is lost: hesitating; jumping the gun; not predefining risk; defining risk but refusing to take the loss (letting it become a bigger loser); exiting a winning trade too soon; taking no profits from a winner; letting a winner turn into a loser; moving a stop closer to entry; getting stopped out then watching price revert; trading too large relative to equity.
trigger_invalidation: Framework; no market thesis.
risk_geometry: None. These are the failure modes the regime structurally prevents (predefined risk, rigid exits, no stop editing).
quote: you become susceptible to committing all the typical trading errors (hesitating, jumping the gun, not predefining your risk, defining your risk but refusing to take the loss and letting the trade turn into a bigger loser, getting out of a winning trade too soon, not taking any profits out of a winning trade, letting a winning trade turn into a loser, moving a stop closer to your entry point...)
chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Objectivity and the error list

strategy_name: No out-of-parameter information in trade selection
mechanism: adding extra variables to the entry decision corrupts the edge definition and destroys the ability to know what works
setup_summary: The only evidence used to decide whether to take a trade is whether the edge's defining variables are present; gathering 'other' evidence (indicators, friends' opinions, broker tips) adds random variables and makes it impossible to determine what works. The book ties this to traders who plan trades, skip them, and instead act on tips — i.e., unstructured random trading that escapes responsibility.
trigger_invalidation: Violated whenever an Expert's decision path consumes information outside its frozen feature groups.
risk_geometry: n/a — decision hygiene, not entry geometry.
quote: When you use "other" information, outside the parameters of your edge to decide whether you will take the trade, you are adding random variables to your trading regime.

strategy_name: Projected support/resistance levels are fragile; one large order can break any level
mechanism: a single large market order can negate any projected level, so level-based invalidation must always be paired with predefined risk rather than trusted as a boundary
setup_summary: Anchored by the soybean anecdote: an analyst projected 'support = low of the day' using the point-and-line method, and a 40-year floor veteran selling 2 million bushels at market broke the level in 30 seconds. Claim: from an individual observer's perspective 'anything can happen, and it takes only one trader to do it'; levels are expressions of belief, not boundaries, and any trader can change them.
trigger_invalidation: n/a — a risk framing: never rely on a level holding as the sole protection; when a level breaks, the dead-thesis trigger fires and the predefined stop is honored.
risk_geometry: Stop placement: levels are fragile anchors for entries, not guarantees; risk predefinition (NEW_predefined_risk) is the protection, and a level break is a dead-thesis trigger, not an 'impossible' event.
quote: anything can happen, and it takes only one trader to do it
chapter_anchor: Ch 6, 'The Uncertainty Principle' (soybean support/resistance anecdote)
notes: Related to stop_hunt and liquidity-sweep dynamics: in perp crypto, obvious levels concentrate stop liquidity and leverage cascades break them mechanically. This is the supporting rationale for V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim (wick through a windowed prior extreme) and for never treating a frozen level as guaranteed.

strategy_name: Order-flow informativeness (inventory-control / hot-potato microstructure)
mechanism: Completed order flow carries information independent of the news behind it; dealer inventory balancing and large directional client orders move short-term price
setup_summary: Aggregated aggressive (taker) buy minus sell flow over a lookback window is a feature with predictive drift beyond bar direction: 'order flow is itself informative.' Book describes three channels: inventory control effect (dealer adjusts spread to shed unwanted inventory), hot potato effect (unwanted position passed around, price bid up/down repeatedly), and asymmetric information effect (large directional client order read as informed, dealer widens).
trigger_invalidation: Feature, not a standalone entry: signal = sustained flow imbalance in one direction; invalidates when flow flips or price diverges from flow (absorption).
risk_geometry: Feature input only; no entry/stop geometry in the book - it is an informational feature to stack with price-based entries.
quote: Market microstructure analyses have found that order flow is an important variable in exchange rate determination in that it is unique from the information that underlies it. In other words, the order flow is itself informative.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Market Microstructure Analysis' p.77
notes: Book cites empirical microstructure findings (dealer flow as short-term price driver). On perp venues taker-flow imbalance is observable in aggTrades, but V8's canonical 1h OHLCV tape has no order-level data - so this lands as a feature-group proposal (aggregated taker-flow imbalance per bar) contingent on tape extension, not an executable expert now.

strategy_name: Limit-order bias and fast-market patience (execution tactics)
setup_summary: Prefer limit orders over market orders: place the order at the lower end of the random quote 'bounce' for buys to get better fills and less slippage. In fast markets liquidity dries up, the spread widens, and market orders fill at the extreme of the move; the Turtles waited for some indication of at least a temporary reversal before entering, and exited via limit or market order once the market stabilized even if price had traded past the stop level. Stops were never placed with brokers (position concealment), only tracked as prices.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — execution methodology.
risk_geometry: Entry/exit fill rules only; no stop, target, or expiry changes.
quote: The idea behind using limit orders is to place your order at the lower end of the bounce instead of simply placing a market order... Market orders placed into a fast market usually end up getting filled at the highest price of the run-up, right at the point where the market begins to stabilize as new sellers come in.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Tactics' and 'Fast Markets', pp. 268-270
notes: V8's canonical simulator fills at close, so intra-bar bounce/limit execution is not modeled; this lesson informs slippage assumptions in the cost model and any live implementation (perp taker fees make limit fills a real cost edge). The fast-market reversal observation ('new sellers come in, price stabilizes and reverses') is a microstructure claim relevant to liquidation-cascade regimes.

strategy_name: Liquidity-first market selection; avoid illiquid instruments
setup_summary: Trade only the most liquid markets: liquidity was the primary criterion for market selection because large positions in thin markets move price so much that entries and exits incur unacceptable losses. Trade a broad enough set to catch trends, but never trade illiquid markets or trade chosen markets inconsistently.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — market-selection rule.
risk_geometry: N/A.
quote: The Turtles traded only the most liquid markets. In fact, market liquidity was the primary criterion Richard Dennis used when determining which markets we were to trade.

strategy_name: Support/resistance breakdown continuation (the trend-following edge at S/R failure)
mechanism: When support/resistance breaks down there is a 'gap in human perception' - holders cling to stale beliefs, no new buyers appear below the level, and selling begets selling, so the market moves farther after a breakdown than at other times (liquidity vacuum below the level)
setup_summary: Buy resistance breakdowns to enter longs, sell support breakdowns to enter shorts: when the close breaks below a windowed prior low that was previously defended (heating-oil example: Sept 5 close below the Aug 30 low at $2.05 after Support 1 and Support 2 held earlier), there is no obvious subsequent anchor, so the move continues long and hard; entry is on/just after the breakdown close. The book asserts a statistically significant tendency for larger moves after S/R breakdowns.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close through a prior extreme after prior tests of that level. Invalidation for the trend side: none beyond the exit rule - this is the continuation edge (failed breakout = entry, not fade); countertrend side must not fight the breakdown.
risk_geometry: entry: bar close at breakdown (or next open, limit orders to avoid adverse fill); stop: ~2N (Turtle) or a small buffer beyond the broken level; target: none (trend continuation); expiry: none.
quote: A breakout occurs when the price 'breaks out' of previous resistance and support levels. As breakout traders, we were buying resistance breakdowns to enter long trades and selling support breakdowns to enter short trades.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Falling Off the Edge (pp.79-82)
notes: Directly corroborates V8's existing failed_breakout family (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry, behavior failed_breakout_reentry): the book generalizes it to both directions (V8's current expert is SHORT-only) and supplies the psychological mechanism (anchoring/recency/disposition creating the perception gap). The 'statistically significant' claim is asserted, not quantified in Part 1. Perp: liquidation cascades amplify the vacuum, but fill-at-close entry may chase fast moves; frozen prior_high_ref already matches the book's frozen-anchor approach.

strategy_name: Springs and Upthrusts (Wyckoff false breaks / stop hunts)
mechanism: liquidity_vacuum_reentry - a false break below support (spring) or above resistance (upthrust) runs the stops and traps the momentum participants on the wrong side; the reclaim on a close proves the defending side (bulls at support, bears at resistance) is victorious.
setup_summary: Spring (LONG): price breaks under a tested horizontal support and then closes back above it (new lows could not hold); buy the reclaim. Upthrust (SHORT): price penetrates a tested horizontal resistance and then closes back under it; sell the failure. Ideal volume: light on the break, heavier on the reclaim.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back above the broken support (spring) / close back under the broken resistance (upthrust). Invalidation: a close back through the most recent swing low (spring) or recent swing high (upthrust) voids the thesis and the target; a beachhead maintained (holding above broken resistance) means bulls keep control.
risk_geometry: Stop = most recent swing low (spring, preferably on a close); target = the high before the spring was made or the top of the trading range; upthrust target = recent low or bottom of range; entry on the reclaim close.
quote: a spring develops when the market breaks under a horizontal support area and then springs back above that previously broken support... If the market is solid, it should not get back to the most recent lows. That would be a stop level (preferably on a close).
chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Candles with Trend Lines - Springs and Upthrusts, pp. 199-205
notes: Direct, named support for the V8 failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim families - stop hunts above/below ranges are endemic to leveraged crypto. Adds a participation refinement (light break / heavy reclaim volume) and explicit target semantics (pre-spring high or range top) to the existing frozen-ref design.

strategy_name: Shakeout probe below support precedes successful breakout
mechanism: A brief probe below an obvious support level or trendline shakes out weak hands and absorbs overhead supply; reclaiming the level within a few days leaves less supply to block the next breakout, so the probe-reclaim is structurally bullish.
setup_summary: In the days before a successful breakout, the instrument undercuts a prior low or trendline support by a small margin, holds below for no more than a few days, and snaps back above it (FXI July-2005 gap below its base then reclaim, XHB Sept-2006 undercut of prior low then breakout 3 days later, SMH Jan-2005 one-week probe below weekly uptrend line, OIH inverted-hammer shakeout before breakout). Buy the subsequent breakout of the consolidation. Note the book also uses stop hunts to explain why entry orders placed only a few pennies above a prior high trigger prematurely - market makers/specialists push price just past the level to grab shares before reversal.
trigger_invalidation: Failure to reclaim above the probed level within a few days means the break was a real breakdown (trend reversal), not a shakeout; do not blindly buy every dip below support - wait for reclaim confirmation.
risk_geometry: entry: breakout above the consolidation high after probe-reclaim (or reclaim above trendline); stop: below the probe low; target: new highs; expiry: days.
quote: When an ETF moves marginally below a pivotal level of support for no more than a few days, and then promptly zooms back above it, it has the effect of shaking out the weak hands... This has the corresponding effect of absorbing a large amount of what would have been overhead supply.
chapter_anchor: Ch.9 FXI, SMH, XHB trade examples + Ch.7 'stop hunts' (probes past highs/lows by market makers)
notes: This is the V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim mechanism; wick-based sweeps of liquidations/stop clusters are native to 24/7 leveraged crypto. The perp venue has no specialist, but clustered stop levels and liquidation cascades play the same role.

strategy_name: Swing-high/low trailing stops with 2:1 minimum reward/risk
mechanism: Trailing stops just beyond swing highs/lows (with padding against stop hunts) lock in the bulk of a move without giving it all back; a 2:1 minimum reward/risk makes a 50% or lower batting average net profitable.
setup_summary: For winners, especially breakouts to new highs (which have no overhead resistance to target), trail the protective stop below each successive swing low (longs) or above each swing high (shorts); move to breakeven after the first structure confirms (OIH: break of May low -> stop to breakeven, then trail above each bounce high). Never set stops exactly at swing levels - add padding (~15-20c intraday, ~1 point daily) against stop hunts. For short-term setups the minimum reward/risk is 2:1 on every entry. Exception: parabolic high-volume exhaustion moves (upper trend-channel probe + volume spike, e.g. IYR Feb-2007) - sell into strength rather than trail, because such moves mark at least a short-term top. Exit basis: trendline breaks on the trade's timeframe (hourly for short-term, daily/weekly for longer holds); a legitimate break shows a volume spike with a large down candle, minor probes without volume get more leeway.
trigger_invalidation: A high-volume, big-candle break of the trailing line/structure = legitimate reversal, stop should have been hit; double-bottom or double-top structure near the stop warrants tightening (lock in gains).
risk_geometry: entry: per setup; stop: padded swing extreme then trailing structure; target: none for new-high trades (stop-managed), prior high/low for others; expiry: none (stop-managed).
quote: you always set the stop about 15 to 20 cents above on an intraday chart, or a point above on a daily chart, which prevents the stop from getting triggered before you want it to by the specialists and market makers.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Trailing Stops' (OIH trailing example, IYR parabolic), Ch.6 reward/risk rule (SPY H&S ~2:1 'minimum ratio to look for with all long and short setups')
notes: Swing-high/low trailing with padding is directly implementable on BTCUSDT 1h and aligns with V8's risk_geometry (stop/target/expiry) and lifecycle exits. Padding rationale survives venue transfer: stop clusters at round numbers and swing extremes exist in perps even without designated market makers.

strategy_name: Spring and Upthrust — false break and reclaim (change of polarity)
mechanism: false breakdown/breakout through a horizontal congestion boundary that fails to hold, then reclaim through the 'broken' level = trap; target back to the opposite end of the range
setup_summary: Spring (long): prices break under horizontal congestion support then spring back above the 'broken' support — bullish, with a measured target to the upper end of the congestion band. Upthrust (short): prices break above a resistance line from a lateral zone, fail to hold, and pull back under the 'broken' resistance — target is a retest of the lower end of the recent trading zone.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: penetration of a horizontal boundary that fails to hold (close reclaims the boundary). Invalidation: the break holds on a close (a genuine breakout — see the donchian_breakout family).
risk_geometry: Entry on the reclaim close; stop on the failed-break extreme (below the spring low / above the upthrust high); target = opposite end of the congestion band; old support converts to resistance (change of polarity).
quote: Spring When prices break under the support of a horizontal congestion band and then springs back above the 'broken support' area. This is bullish and there is a measured price target to the upper end of the congestion band.

strategy_name: Failed breakout short (overhead resistance)
mechanism: a failed breakout above a consolidation with overhead resistance leaves trapped bulls and a liquidity vacuum that pulls price back down through the level
setup_summary: Daily: after price breaks above a multi-week consolidation/prior high, it closes back below that level (breakout failure), ideally making a lower high; enter short on the break of a confirmatory level such as the 50-day MA or the prior day's low. Target is the prior swing low; stop above the failed-breakout extreme.

strategy_name: Round-number trigger and stop placement
mechanism: orders cluster at psychologically salient whole numbers, so price probes just beyond them before reversing and clustered stops at round levels get run
setup_summary: Set buy triggers just below the whole number and sell/exit limits just above it (e.g. sell at 48.98, not 49.00); never set protective stops exactly at whole numbers.
trigger_invalidation: Placement rule, not an entry signal; ignore if fills prove unreliable.
risk_geometry: Trigger/exit offsets of a few cents from round numbers improve fill odds.

strategy_name: No-free-lunch cost-side accounting (gamma/theta/vega symmetry)
mechanism: every convexity or carry advantage carries a symmetric cost - long-gamma pays theta and bleeds on IV decline; short-gamma collects theta but carries unlimited move/IV-spike tail risk
setup_summary: Methodology lesson: strategies that appear to profit from the mere passage of time (short premium: 'what could be more certain than time passing?') or from movement in every direction (long premium) carry a mirrored cost. Long-gamma positions pay theta every day and are exposed to IV declines ('death of a thousand cuts'); short-gamma positions are exposed to large moves and IV spikes that can wipe out accumulated time-decay income in one bar. The cost side must be quantified and factored into the forecast before the trade.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - methodology lesson; informs position sizing, regime gating, and the decision to carry versus exit; applies before entry.
risk_geometry: Cost-side budgeting at selection; the theta/gamma mirror images (Figures 4.10 and 4.12) imply time-based discipline for convexity longs and hard stops for convexity shorts.
quote: The bottom line is that there is no free lunch with straddles and strangles. For every upside there is a downside, and the risks have to be understood, factored into the forecast, and properly managed in a disciplined fashion.

notes: Directly relevant to V8's funding-carry and carry-negative experts: perp funding plays the theta role, so a long-position-paying-funding thesis must budget carry the same way the book budgets theta, and a funding-collecting thesis must budget the liquidation/expansion tail.
