strategy_name: Systematic rule execution over discretion ('rules beat judgment')
mechanism: rule_based_execution: a hired hand forced to follow exact rules outperforms a discretionary expert relying on intuition; teachable process dominates innate skill.
setup_summary: Encode the strategy fully as rules and execute them exactly, with no discretion; the transferability claim is that any operator following the exact rules matches or beats the originator.
trigger_invalidation: Not a trade setup; it is the thesis that rule-adherence (not judgment) drives the track record.
risk_geometry: None stated.
quote: I think I could take a kid who wasn't my son and say, 'Do this, I'll pay you $50,000 a year, or you're fired if you don't exactly follow it.' He'd beat me every day, every week, every month and every year.
chapter_anchor: Ch.14 'Model Greatness' epigraph, Tom Willis (p.187)
notes: Validates V8's architecture (behavior families as fully specified falsifiable rule sets, no discretion in replay); no new strategy.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Volatility expansion breakout (backspread as long-vol expression)
mechanism: Low-volatility compression with falling IV is a pre-breakout state; the phase ends with a high-velocity directional move that a long-gamma structure (or, in perp terms, a breakout entry) monetizes.
setup_summary: On BTC 1h: identify a low-volatility consolidation (narrow range, ATR/range contracting over N bars, often with declining volume) between defined support/resistance; if a close occurs beyond the range boundary (the 'breakout/acceleration zone'), enter in the breakout direction with the expectation of a high-magnitude, short-timeframe continuation. Short strike/backstop anchored at the broken S/R level; target zone is the forecast acceleration area.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond range boundary after sustained compression. Invalidation: no breakout within the forecast horizon (time stop — book: 'if by the close of business Friday the move has not taken place, he should exit'); price re-enters the range (failed breakout); momentum stalls at old S/R.
risk_geometry: Entry: breakout bar close (perp analog of long-strike capture); stop: back below the broken boundary (the short strike is 'backstopped by support or resistance'); target: projected acceleration zone; expiry: expiry cycle tied to forecast breakout time, 'buy extra time' (longer expiry) if timing is uncertain; time and price stops both mandatory.
quote: Backspreads, also known as volatility spreads... are used to capture high-magnitude, high-velocity directional moves occurring in a short time frame.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 Strategy Overview + Investment Objectives, pp. 223, 238-241
notes: Book frames the trade as buying OTM options financed by an ATM sale; the V8-relevant core is the falsifiable volatility-regime claim (compression precedes expansion) plus the strike rule 'short strike backstopped by support/resistance, long strike in the acceleration zone', which maps to stop placement beyond the compressed range on a perp.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Trading Rule 1: predefine what a loss is in every trade
mechanism: Predefining the market condition that invalidates a trade removes weighing and judging at exit time, letting a loss be executed as an automatic function of the strategy instead of negotiated under pain.
setup_summary: Before entry, specify exactly what the market must look like or do to prove the trade no longer represents an opportunity in the trading timeframe; the loss is defined by an observable market condition, not by dollar pain. This is the book's first formal trading rule.
trigger_invalidation: The predefined invalidation condition IS the thesis-killer: if it occurs, exit. The book warns that failing to execute it on a winner reinforces inappropriate behavior that 'will inevitably lead to disaster'.
risk_geometry: No entry; a pre-entry loss definition. Maps to V8 risk_geometry invalidation and the still_valid dead-thesis exit (a separate exit from the stop-loss).
quote: Predefine what a loss is in every potential trade.
chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Two: Dealing with Losses - Trading Rule 1', p.170
notes: This is the book's clearest articulation of V8's dead-thesis/still_valid concept and its separation from the stop-loss: the loss is defined by what the market does, not by price distance. Corroborated across the psychology/craft books in the library.
book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

strategy_name: Trading Rule 2: execute losing trades immediately upon perception
mechanism: Hesitating on a predefined loss either reinforces bad behavior (when it recovers) or starts a pain spiral (when it worsens); immediate execution keeps the trader available for the next opportunity and prevents compounding errors like skipping the next trade or chasing tips.
setup_summary: Upon perception that a trade is a predefined loser, exit immediately with no consideration, weighing, or judgment; if you find yourself weighing, the loss was either not predefined or not being executed. Book's second formal trading rule.
trigger_invalidation: Exit rule, not a setup. Failure modes the book names: letting the loss worsen, then not taking the next opportunity ('which invariably is always a winning trade'), then anger-driven tip-taking ('which invariably is always a loser').
risk_geometry: Exit discipline complementing the stop-loss with a dead-thesis exit; no entry or target; 'keep your contract size light' until flawless execution is second nature.
quote: Execute your losing trades immediately upon perception that they exist.
chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Two: Dealing with Losses - Trading Rule 2', pp.170-171
notes: In perp crypto with high leverage this discipline is what separates a controlled loss from liquidation; the book frames it as protecting future decision-making, not just capital. Maps to V8 RiskGate/deterministic admission and the simulator's STOP_FIRST semantics.
book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

strategy_name: Springs and Upthrusts (Wyckoff false-breakout return)
mechanism: unsustained penetration of a range extreme creates a vacuum: price returns to the opposite side of the congestion band
setup_summary: In a lateral range, price momentarily pierces a prior low (spring) or breaches a prior high (upthrust) but the penetration is unsustained (no durable close through). Spring: buy on reclaim above the old lows, objective is retest of the upper band, stop under the spring-day low. Upthrust: short once the new high fails to hold, objective is retest of the lower band, stop above the new high. The book explicitly states the target (opposite end of the trading range) and protective stop (the new high/low of the false breakout) for both. Confluence with a candlestick signal (shooting star on the upthrust day, hammer on the spring day) strengthens the entry.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: intraday breach of a prior extreme that does not hold on a close basis (the book's beachhead rule: bulls must CLOSE above resistance and then hold old resistance as new support; intra-day pushes are not enough). Invalidation: sustained close through the level, or (for upthrust) the market establishing camp in enemy territory.
risk_geometry: Entry: on the reclaim/close back inside the range (book: buy if prices push back above the old lows). Stop: under the spring-day low (spring) or above the new high made on the false breakout (upthrust). Target: the opposite end of the congestion band. No expiry stated.
quote: Trading springs and upthrusts is so effective because they provide a clear target (the opposite end of the trading range) and protective stop (the new high or low made with the 'false breakout').
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Candlesticks with Trendlines - Springs and Upthrusts' pp.193-200 (also scouting-party/beachhead discussion p.199-201)
notes: This is direct corroboration of two existing V8 families: the spring is liquidity_sweep_reclaim (wick through prior low reclaimed by close) and the upthrust is failed_breakout (close below windowed prior high after failed breakout). The book adds explicit, concrete risk geometry: stop beyond the false-breakout extreme, target = opposite side of the range. In leveraged 24/7 crypto, stop-run sweeps of prior 1h/4h highs and lows are pervasive, so the close-based beachhead confirmation ('it is a close above' - Ch.1 p.7) is the load-bearing rule to keep.
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

strategy_name: Spring (false breakdown) and upthrust (false breakout) at congestion bands
mechanism: stop-run under/over a congestion band creates a vacuum; close-based reclaim signals the trapped side is wrong
setup_summary: In a lateral congestion band, prices undercut band support and then close back above it (spring = bullish), or push above band resistance and close back below it (upthrust = bearish). The reclaim must hold on a close; the book repeatedly requires close-based hold of the broken level before acting (corn: hammer holding $2.65 support on a close).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back on the reclaimed side of a broken congestion-band edge after an undercut/overthrow. Invalidated if price closes back through the reclaimed edge toward the failed side.
risk_geometry: Entry on reclaim-bar close (book buys next session after confirmation); stop beyond the undercut low (spring) or failed high (upthrust); target = opposite side of the congestion band or the prior range boundary.
quote: Spring—when prices break under the support of a horizontal congestion band and then springs back above the 'broken support' area. This is bullish.
chapter_anchor: Glossary B 'Spring'/'Upthrust' (pp. 303-307); Ch. 20 corn Exhibit 20.4, p. 285; Ch. 20 crude/silver examples
notes: Directly corroborates V8's formalized liquidity_sweep_reclaim family. Adds two refinements: (1) congestion-band context (sweeps are traded only at band edges, not at arbitrary extremes) and (2) close-based hold confirmation before the reclaim is trusted (matches V8's still_valid/reclaim semantics).
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

strategy_name: Kangaroo Tail zone sweep-reclaim
mechanism: A long wick through a zone that closes back on the zone's other side shows the level was probed and rejected, sweeping resting stops and leaving reversal fuel.
setup_summary: Single candle on a zone with open and close in the extreme third of the candle (top third bullish, bottom third bearish), a long tail relative to the body, open and close inside the previous candle's range (market not in a runaway phase), and ideally a range greater than the previous 10 candles. Most such candles penetrate the zone intra-bar, then close back on the other side. Enter via a stop beyond the tail end; emergency stop a few pips beyond the tail; target the next zone.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme-third open+close, long tail, open/close inside prior candle range, printed on a zone. Invalidation: stop a few pips beyond the tail; the book also recommends closing early if the drawdown reaches 75% of the way to the stop. Red flags: short tails, no zone, giant candles immediately prior, or open/close outside the prior candle's range.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop a few pips above the high (bullish) / sell stop below the low (bearish). Stop: a few pips beyond the tail (maximum loss). Optional early exit at 75% of the distance to the stop. Target: next zone.
quote: Most kangaroo tails will push through the zone and then come back and close on the other side of the zone.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Kangaroo Tails' pp.131-150 (tips and red flags pp.149-150)
notes: Nearly identical to V8's formalized liquidity_sweep_reclaim (wick through windowed prior extreme reclaimed by close, frozen ref, stay-on-reclaimed-side still_valid). The book's tail-vs-body length, extreme-third open/close, and prior-range filters are concrete candidate variant refinements; 'room to the left' supports the windowed-extreme reference.
book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

strategy_name: Multi-touch trendline break as high-conviction support violation
mechanism: a support line touched multiple times concentrates order flow; a decisive close through it is a major regime signal, not a noise event
setup_summary: Fit an up-trendline to at least three swing lows; a decisive close below the multi-touch line is a major sell signal (book example: break of a four-year, three-touch support line caught the consumer discretionary decline one-third in). Falsifiable: breaks of >=3-touch trendlines lead larger and longer moves than breaks of 1-2 touch lines.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close below a >=3-touch rising trendline. Invalidation: close reclaims the trendline side within K bars (trap) or the trendline was fit on <3 touches.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close through the trendline. Stop: trendline reclaim / swing extreme. Target: not stated; book notes the break occurred only a third into the decline, implying large residual move.
quote: The more times a trendline is touched, the more reliable it becomes. A good trendline should be touched at least three times as this one was. That's why the decisive break of that four-year support line during October 2007 (circle) was so important.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11, 'Consumer Discretionary Breakdown' (fig 11.3); also Ch 11 fig 11.11 (RTPIX trendline breaks)
notes: The '>=3 touches' reliability rule is a concrete, testable feature for the location feature group and for supply_demand_zone-type logic. Trendline fitting is subjective; V8 would need a deterministic fit (e.g., anchored least-squares or pivot-based). In 24/7 crypto, hourly trendlines are noisy and high leverage makes stop placement sensitive to fit method.

strategy_name: Forced-selling cascade exhaustion
mechanism: mechanical stop-losses and forced liquidation selling beget further selling; once the forced-seller population is exhausted, the non-leveraged patient side can buy the dislocation
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: a sharp collapse amplified by forced selling (liquidation cascade - OI purge, forced-long liquidation spike, price sweeping a cluster of prior stops) followed by a bar-close reclaim back above the cascade extreme = long setup. The buyer who is not forced to sell can wait out the volatility.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis is that the decline was forced-selling-driven, not structural. Invalidated if price keeps printing new cascade lows with fresh liquidation waves (secular decline, not exhaustion) - ties to the value-trap rule.
risk_geometry: Entry on bar close reclaim of the cascade low; stop below cascade extreme (swing/ATR); target prior congestion; expiry in bars; dead-thesis if new cascade lows.
quote: this strategy—which is simply an exotically-labeled version of the small speculator's stop-loss order—dictates that ever-increasing portions of a stock portfolio, or their index-future equivalents, be sold as prices decline
chapter_anchor: Part II.C Debunking Standard Dogma (1987), pp. 81-82 (portfolio insurance / Brady Report $60-90B on a hair trigger)
notes: Refines the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family: distinguishes forced-selling exhaustion from secular decline. Perp-specific: no circuit breakers, 24/7, liquidation engines, and high leverage guarantee forced sellers exist on every crash.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Momentum-stall leverage fragility (price need not fall, only stop rising fast)
mechanism: Leveraged credit is only solvent while the collateralizing asset keeps appreciating; deceleration of appreciation — not a decline — is sufficient to trigger defaults and cascades, because payments and margins were built on the extrapolated appreciation.
setup_summary: Falsifiable regime claim from Lippmann's quant evidence: when price appreciation decelerates from an extended fast-appreciation regime while leverage (OI, funding-heavy positioning) is high, treat as a fragile regime. The empirical anchor: since 2000, homes appreciating only 1-5% defaulted at nearly 4x the rate of homes appreciating >10%; first-year subprime defaults had already risen from 1% to 4% while prices still rose, and 8% pool losses zeroed the triple-B tranches.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: measured deceleration of appreciation below the prior regime rate with elevated leverage. Invalidated if a sustained price stall does not produce rising forced liquidation/default rates within the observation window.
risk_geometry: Regime filter for RiskGate admission and long-side still_valid gating; no entry/stop/target of its own.
quote: Home prices didn't even need to fall. They merely needed to stop rising at the unprecedented rates they had the previous few years for vast numbers of Americans to default on their home loans.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'How Can a Guy Who Can't Speak English Lie?' (Lippmann's 'Shorting Home Equity Mezzanine Tranches' pitch)
notes: The book makes a falsifiable statistical case (specific 4x multiplier, 1%->4% first-year default, 7%/8% pool-loss thresholds zeroing BBB-/BBB). Perp leverage is marked continuously, so the stall-to-cascade mechanism is the core of crypto liquidation cascades and transfers more directly than the mortgage reset mechanics. Reuses starter slug deleveraging_cascade.
book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

strategy_name: Trading into profile holes (minus development)
mechanism: low-volume-at-price regions (holes, 'minus development') between areas of horizontal development lack technical support, so price traverses them fast and with high reward-to-risk
setup_summary: Build a rolling volume-at-price distribution over a lookback window; identify holes = price ranges where volume did not accumulate (no horizontal development). When price breaks from a balanced area toward a hole, expect a rapid vertical traversal to the far side (next high-volume area). Long: enter near the unfair low only when a short-timeframe pause forms (new small Dynamic VAP = supporting volume); Short: enter on a break below the balance support with stop above the breakdown bar.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price breaks the edge of a balanced area toward a profile hole. Invalidation: quick probe failure inside the hole - the book's 'Probe' bars fail fast, so a failed probe allows a tight stop; reversal back into the balance area invalidates.
risk_geometry: Entry at the hole edge (pause-confirmed) or on the break bar close; stop just beyond the breakdown level / above the breakdown-bar high; targets = far side of the hole (opposite HVA), then the far end of that HVA; reward-to-risk is claimed higher than horizontal trades provided you are on the correct side.
quote: These rapid vertical moves are caused by supply/demand imbalances and, in profile terms, this leaves a hole in the profile that, when revisited, has a high probability for fast price movement.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 240-245) 'Vertical Nondevelopment (Minus Development)', Figures 5.16-5.17; Trading Application #1 (pp. 275-278, Gold)
notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7 with venue aggregate volume available, so volume-at-price profiles are computable, but aggregate-tape noise (HFT wash, funding-driven flow) makes the 'hole' definition venue- and lookback-sensitive - hence MEDIUM. The mechanism (vacuum traversal) is closely allied to the existing liquidity_vacuum_reentry family; new-family registry decision required. Feature input: volume-at-price sparsity in a price band.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Five-player breakout liquidity accumulation
mechanism: on a range breakout the four participant groups respond asymmetrically (novice sellers panic-cover at any cost, pro-sellers' tight stops convert to buying, pro-buyers add), so volume-at-price becomes one-sided and each successive prior pivot extreme taken out adds more one-sided flow - a self-reinforcing liquidity run
setup_summary: On a breakout from a balance area, expect volume to become one-sided in the breakout direction (all or most of the volume moves to one side). Feature proposal: measure volume-at-price asymmetry at the breakout edge and the accumulation of one-sided volume as each successive prior pivot high/low is exceeded; wider-range non-overlapping bars confirm the flow. This fuels breakout follow-through and is the mechanism behind fast vertical moves.
trigger_invalidation: Feature/mechanism input, not a standalone trigger. If volume does not become one-sided on breakout (balanced volume, quick failure), the breakout lacks the fuel for vertical continuation - a confirmation filter for breakout-family entries.
risk_geometry: N/A (feature) - feeds the liquidity_sweep_reclaim / failed_breakout / hole-traversal mechanisms and breakout follow-through confidence.
quote: The most remarkable part of this breakout is what is significant: all (or most) of the volume in this timeframe moves to one side of the market; in this example, to the upside.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 228-231) 'Four Market Participants--and Then a Fifth', Figure 5.11
notes: In perps the counterpart of 'novice sellers panic-covering' is liquidation cascades + stop-runs, so the mechanism maps strongly, but one-sidedness must be measured on venue aggregate volume with wash-trade noise - hence MEDIUM. Proposed feature: breakout-direction volume share (volume-at-price asymmetry) as a participation-group feature usable by liquidity families.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Pre-committed mechanical order execution (plan then trade)
mechanism: Placing entry and protective orders ahead of the session removes in-the-moment hesitation, fear, and greed from execution; the process runs mechanically regardless of the trader's emotional state.
setup_summary: Do the analysis in a calm, undisturbed state (the author writes entries/exits on the weekend); place GTC entry and stop-loss orders before the session; then sit back - winners run, losers get stopped, and un-hit orders are cancelled at the horizon end. The book's worksheets add a defined risk factor and profit objective to every pre-placed order.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - an execution methodology rule.
risk_geometry: Pre-placed entry + stop + target as a bracket; orders cancelled at period end if unfilled.
quote: On Monday mornings I place open orders (GTC) for clients based on that research, both entry and stop-loss orders. The next step is to sit back and wait. The process is all mechanical; no emotions hinder me.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, 'Your Trading To-Do List' (pp.198-199)
notes: Execution methodology, corroborated across the library's psychology chapters. In 24/7 perps resting orders are the only way to trade unattended sessions, so pre-committed entry/stop/target brackets are the practical analogue of this rule. Reinforces V8's pre-planned risk_geometry (entry/target/stop/expiry fixed at proposal, not ad hoc).
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Buy below intrinsic value (margin-of-safety discount entry / repurchase logic)
mechanism: When market price sits at a wide discount to an independently-estimated fair value, buying returns $2 of present value for $1; the auction nature of security markets lets the buyer acquire value at a fraction of negotiated-acquisition prices.
setup_summary: Define an anchor independent of price — for perps, a synthetic fair value such as a funding/carry-adjusted equilibrium or a realized-volatility-based valuation band. When price trades below anchor by a margin-of-safety threshold, enter LONG; when above by the same threshold, enter SHORT. Falsifiable: fixed discount threshold, fixed convergence horizon, stop below the discount-defining structural extreme.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = discount-to-anchor exceeds the margin-of-safety threshold; invalidation = the anchor itself is repriced (fair value revision, e.g., funding regime change) or price fails to converge to anchor within the holding horizon, proving the discount was not a mispricing.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close or limit at the discount level; stop beyond the structural extreme defining the discount; target = reversion to anchor (structure, not fixed R); long expiry because convergence is slow.
quote: major repurchases at prices well below per-share intrinsic business value immediately increase, in a highly significant way, that value. When companies purchase their own stock, they often find it easy to get $2 of present value for $1.
chapter_anchor: Part IV.A Sensible Stock Repurchases Versus Greenmail, p.147
notes: Only genuinely actionable strategy family in this part. Crypto perps have no DCF intrinsic value, so the strategy is implementable only with an explicit synthetic anchor (funding/carry equilibrium or vol band); absent an anchor it is unfalsifiable. The 'auction market vs negotiated price' point maps to perp microstructure: continuous two-sided auction lets a patient buyer accumulate at auction-clearing discounts that a negotiated (market-order) purchase cannot get.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Oops gap-fade (stop-entry through the prior extreme after a gap open)
mechanism: a gap open beyond the prior extreme is an emotional overshoot of the chasing crowd; when price trades back through the prior extreme it traps those orders and reverses, so entering via a stop through the extreme exploits the trapped flow
setup_summary: When a market gaps below the prior session low, place a BUY stop a few ticks above the prior low; when it gaps above the prior high, place a SELL stop a few ticks below the prior high. The stop triggers on reclaim of the prior extreme. Larry Williams' method; works best in countertrend conditions (e.g., sell-oops in an uptrend). The stop entry also protects against a true breakaway gap (new valuation).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: gap open through a prior session extreme, then price trades back through the extreme triggering the stop. Thesis invalidation: the gap is a genuine breakaway (no reclaim); price reclaims but fails to follow through (double-invalidation).
risk_geometry: entry = stop order just beyond the prior extreme (buy stop above prior low / sell stop below prior high); stop = a few ticks on the far side; target = gap fill / countertrend distance; expiry = intraday, at most 1-2 sessions ('If you were to hold this position more than one day without proper stop or risk management, a nice short-term trade could have resulted in a loss').
quote: When a market opens lower than the previous day's low, a trader should place a buy stop a few ticks above the previous day's low... These reactions tend to work better in countertrend conditions.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5, 'Oops Signal'
notes: True session gaps are rare in 24/7 BTCUSDT (no overnight close), so raw applicability is limited; however the mechanism - price opens beyond a prior extreme then reclaims it, trapping the chasers - is exactly the existing failed_breakout / liquidity_sweep_reclaim family. Recommend treating the oops as a gap-open VARIANT of those experts (an entry-with-stop refinement), not a new family.
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Stop-Run Cascade (clustered stop-loss logic becomes a doomsday machine)
mechanism: when many participants share identical stop-loss logic, triggering one stop auto-triggers the next - the shared logic converts a small move into a self-feeding cascade ('pouring gas on a fire')
setup_summary: Identical stop/automated-selling logic across many players creates cascades: Black Monday's portfolio insurance was 'a bunch of stop/loss orders, but done automatically... they created a doomsday machine that kept selling and selling.' In perp crypto the analogue is liquidation cascades and stop clusters below key levels. Two implications: (a) do not place your own stop in the obvious cluster where it becomes the harvested liquidity; (b) the cascade itself manufactures the overshoot a liquidity-sweep buyer wants.
trigger_invalidation: The cascade stalls once the automated/forced sellers are exhausted (all stops and liquidations consumed); price reclaims the swept level - the sweep is a harvesting event, not a change in trend.
risk_geometry: Stop location is itself a risk decision: stops should sit at structural levels and outside the crowd's cluster, not in the obvious pool; stop placement must assume the stop may be swept before thesis invalidation.
quote: They created a doomsday machine that kept selling and selling.
chapter_anchor: 2007 'Derivatives and the Crowded Trade' (Black Monday / portfolio-insurance analysis)
notes: Corroborates the liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert (wick through prior extreme, reclaimed by close). Mechanism_family_candidate stop_run_cascade, behavior_family_candidate clustered_stop_harvest. The risk-rule output is the more actionable piece for V8: stop geometry must avoid the obvious cluster.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

strategy_name: Event straddle/strangle: both-sides positioning into scheduled announcements
mechanism: Scheduled high-impact announcements compress range beforehand and force a directional expansion afterward; buying both sides monetizes the expansion without predicting direction
setup_summary: When a market has been moving sideways and a scheduled high-impact event (rate decision, CPI, jobless claims, PPI) approaches, enter both sides simultaneously (buy straddle at-the-money or cheaper OTM strangle); once direction resolves, cut the losing leg immediately and ride the winner, optionally converting the winner to a longer position.
trigger_invalidation: If price never expands (announcement in line, market stays flat), time decay erodes both legs - theta loss is the thesis-invalidator.
risk_geometry: Max loss = initial premium outlay; cut losing leg as soon as direction resolves; strangle preferred when at-the-money vol is rich (book: strangle risked ~1 to gain ~2 on the 397-tick gold example); slippage risk on fast exit.
quote: Instead of forcing an artificial or rumored direction on your trading, use a straddle to establish your initial position.
notes: The straddle vehicle needs an options market V8 does not have (perp-only linear), so the family is DEFER_GATED/backlog. Transferable pieces: pre-event range-compression detection and an event-calendar time feature as FEATURE_INPUT candidates; crypto reacts to CPI/FOMC/ETF decisions with similar expansion but fewer scheduled movers.
book: Trade Like a Pro - 15 High-Profit Trading Strategies 2009
